items_missed: No 'how are you today?' and no real agenda statement - 'we just need to ask you more questions about it if this is a good time' got a confirmation but never told Tim what the call would cover or that it would take 10-15 minutes.
Never asked about packing services. Tim said 'no boxes just that furniture' and she took that as the end of it rather than asking whether he wanted Einstein to pack.
Never asked about additional stops beyond the storage unit.
No 'pricing is super simple' framing before the rate.
Thin what's-included list - named two men, the truck, and the protective wrap, but never said gas, taxes, or insurance are in the rate.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned - no $2,000 accidental damage coverage, on a high-rise move going into long-term storage.

On-Time Guarantee never mentioned - and this was a call where arrival time was the customer's single biggest concern, because new furniture was landing the same day. She said the crew arrives 'between 8:30 and 9:00' and never backed it with the guarantee.
No 'no hidden fees' pitch - named the $75 travel fee but never framed it against no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees.
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check after the clock explanation.
Never asked about specialty items - no piano, safe, or antiques question.

Likely over-quote left uncorrected. She quoted 3.5-5.5 hours, then pushed it to 5-7 for the elevator, on 1 couch, 3 bed frames, 3 mattresses, 4 bar stools, 3 desks, 3 chairs and zero boxes. Tim pushed back directly - 'I don't foresee taking the stuff out taking more than two hours... it's just college furniture stuff, so it's all pretty light' - and she replied 'I can just put it as it is' rather than revising the range.
No Save Your Ass prep speech. She got the 'shorter move, lower cost' idea across but gave no consolidation examples and no carload tip.
Never mentioned that no deposit is required.
No bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email and no reply-with-corrections ask.
Never gave office hours or how to reach the branch.
No insurance explanation at all - neither No Worries nor the 60 cents per pound baseline, on a move into storage.
No Sparefoot mention even though the whole move is a storage job.
top_strength: Excellent access discovery on a hard building, and she closed. She worked the 25th-floor high-rise properly - reserved elevator vs. resident elevator, hundred feet from parking to elevator, school bus equivalent for the hallway run - then carried the same discipline to the storage end (indoor, ground floor, park and walk in). She also caught a cost lever for the customer rather than for herself, noting that a high-rise this size would normally get three movers but two would do for this inventory, and she booked the job on the call for 8:30-9:00 AM Tuesday, the first slot of the day, which was exactly what Tim needed with furniture arriving.
coaching_note: Joanna runs great discovery and closes the booking, but she gave away all four differentiators and then over-quoted the job. When the customer pushed back that it was light college furniture, the right move was to revise the range down on the spot and say why - instead 'I can just put it as it is' locks in a 5-7 hour estimate on a job that may land near three, which is exactly the kind of gap that shows up in our estimate accuracy number. Next call: after the range, ask what he thinks and adjust in front of him, and add the fixed differentiator block - No Worries $2,000, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, no deposit.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and low-friction language throughout - 'no worries', 'that's totally fine', 'thank you so much', 'I hope you have a good day' - she used Tim's name three times and he stayed comfortable and easy the whole way, closing with 'Perfect' and 'sounds good.'
